chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period ('iddah) of the woman who does not menstruate and the woman who has irregular bleeding (mustahadha) and does not become pure is three months. And the waiting period of the woman who menstruates and whose menses are regular is three menstrual cycles. The method for reconciling these narrations is that if it is possible for the mustahadha to know the days of her menstruation, she must observe the cycles that are her pure days. And if it is not possible for her due to the confusion of blood upon her, it suffices for her to observe three months, according to what the last two narrations contained.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman with irregular menstruation who cannot distinguish between menstrual and pure blood?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential method for determining the 'iddah of a mustahadha by distinguishing between those who can identify their natural menstrual cycle and those with irregular bleeding. It establishes a hierarchical legal approach: first, counting three pure days (quru') if menstruation is recognizable, and second, defaulting to a three-month period if the blood is indistinguishable, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in cases of uncertainty.
